### Position read
The opponent opened Red from (0,3) to center (3,3). We answered Blue from (4,7) to (4,4), a center square not immediately sandwichable. Losses remain 0 for every color.
### Our plan
If still safe on Green’s turn, play Green (4,0) to (4,3), securing both lower center squares. Contest rather than rush (3,4): Red at (3,3) plus Red from (0,5) could sandwich a Blue piece placed there by landing at (3,5). Keep same-color flank geometry in mind and protect the central foothold.
### Opponent tendencies
Only one move observed: the opponent prioritized immediate center occupation with Red.
### Lessons
A Blue move to (3,4) would have been vulnerable to Red (0,5)->(3,5), so center entries must be checked against same-color landing flanks.

### Position read
The center is split: opponent pieces at (3,3) Red and (4,3) Yellow; ours at (4,4) Blue. Yellow threatened (7,5)->(4,5), sandwiching Blue (4,4) against Yellow (4,3). Green moved (5,0)->(5,5), blocking that route. Losses remain 0.
### Our plan
Preserve the Blue center foothold and contest (3,4) when it can be supported. Green at (5,5) is a nearby defender/blocker and can reposition along row 5 or column 5. Before each move, check whether the opponent can land opposite one of our pieces using an existing same-color far flank.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent has prioritized central occupation with both colors and immediately formed Yellow sandwich geometry against our Blue center piece.
### Lessons
Threats can be neutralized by blocking the attacking piece’s travel lane when neither the threatened piece nor the intended landing square is movable by the acting color.

### Position read
Blue moved (2,7)->(2,4), sandwiching and capturing Red at (3,4) against Blue at (4,4). Red now has 1 loss. Center after capture: opponent at (3,3) Red and (4,3) Yellow; ours at (4,4) Blue; (3,4) is empty. Green at (5,5) still blocks Yellow’s route from (7,5) to (4,5), protecting Blue (4,4) from a Yellow sandwich against (4,3).
### Our plan
Keep (4,4) occupied and contest (3,4), ideally with support. Preserve the block on column 5 unless another move prevents Yellow from landing at (4,5). Blue at (2,4) and (4,4) create useful same-color vertical geometry around (3,4).
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes the center and formed adjacent same-team occupation quickly. Expect attempts to refill (3,4) or open Yellow’s route to (4,5).
### Lessons
Exploit same-color flanks already embedded near the center; a landing one square beyond an opponent can capture while simultaneously improving central pressure.

### Position read
Red has 1 loss. The center is opponent Red (3,3), opponent Yellow (4,3), our Blue (4,4), with (3,4) empty. Blue (2,4) and (4,4) flank (3,4), but an opponent entering that square is initially safe. Green (5,5) remains essential: moving it off column 5 could let Yellow reach (4,5) and sandwich Blue (4,4) against Yellow (4,3).
### Our plan
Green advanced (3,0)->(3,1), safely staging near the center. Preserve Green (5,5) unless the Yellow sandwich threat is otherwise neutralized. If Red vacates (3,3), look for Green to occupy it; meanwhile Blue should retain (4,4) and contest (3,4). Seek another capture on Red, now at 1 loss.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes central occupation and may move Red from (3,3) to (3,4), or maneuver Yellow to attack Blue (4,4). Expect attempts to dislodge the column-5 blocker.
### Lessons
Central occupation alone is fragile without same-color support. Keep checking whether moving Green (5,5) opens Yellow’s line from (7,5) to (4,5).

### Position read
Red has 1 loss. Center: Red (3,3), Yellow (4,3), our Blue (4,4), and (3,4) empty. Blue moved (2,4)->(2,3), escaping Red’s immediate (3,3)->(2,3) sandwich against Red (2,5) while staying near center. Yellow (5,4) remains available; Green (5,5) blocks Yellow (7,5) from reaching (4,5) to sandwich Blue (4,4).
### Our plan
Preserve Green (5,5) until the Yellow attack on Blue (4,4) is neutralized. Use Blue (2,3) as central support and exploit any vacancy at (3,3) or (4,3). Seek captures on Red, already at 1 loss, without exposing pieces to same-color flanks.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is building central occupation and Red sandwich geometry. Expect Red to shift from (3,3) toward (3,4), while Yellow tries to open the right flank of Blue (4,4).
### Lessons
Before leaving a piece, identify every opponent landing square that completes a same-color sandwich. Do not use a teammate as a blocker if it merely extends a capturable mixed-color line.

### Position read
Losses: Red 1, Green 1, Blue/Yellow 0. Yellow moved (7,6)->(5,6) and sandwiched Green (5,5) against Yellow (5,4). Center remains Red (3,3), Yellow (4,3), Blue (4,4), with (3,4) empty. Blue (4,4) is threatened next Yellow turn by (7,5)->(4,5), using Yellow (4,3) as the far flank. Green redeployed (1,0)->(1,4), safely staging above the open center square.
### Our plan
On Blue’s next turn, neutralize the Yellow sandwich threat to (4,4), preferably while retaining central influence. Green (1,4) can later reach (3,4), but only if Red’s (3,3) plus Red (2,5)->(3,5) cannot sandwich it. Seek captures against Red, already at 1 loss.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is coordinating same-color central flanks: Red around row 2/3 and Yellow across rows 4/5. Expect Red to obstruct or prepare a capture on (3,4), while Yellow continues targeting Blue (4,4).
### Lessons
A vacated blocker can instantly open a long rook landing lane. Before entering (3,4), check both adjacent Red endpoints and every Red piece able to land on the opposite side.

### Position read
Losses: opponent Red 1; our Green 1; others 0. Blue moved (4,4)->(3,4), escaping Yellow’s immediate (7,5)->(4,5) sandwich while retaining one center square. Center is now opponent Red (3,3), our Blue (3,4), opponent Yellow (4,3), and (4,4) empty. Blue (3,4) is currently safe: no Red can immediately land (3,5) or (4,4) to flank it.
### Our plan
On Green’s turn, first handle Green (1,4): opponent Red can play (0,6)->(0,4), sandwiching it against Red (2,4). Move it or obstruct that geometry. Continue denying (4,4); seek a route to reinforce the center without exposing a same-color sandwich. Target Red, already at 1 loss.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent builds same-color flanks around the center. Yellow may occupy (4,4) or reposition from (5,4); Red is likely to exploit the vertical Red–Green–Red setup in column 4.
### Lessons
Central occupation is valuable only when immediate landing squares for opposing same-color flanks are unavailable. Recheck threats after every vacated blocker.

### Position read
Losses: opponent Red 1; our Green 1; others 0. The opponent occupies center squares (3,3), (4,3), and (4,4); our Blue holds (3,4), preventing an immediate center win. Green escaped (1,4), where Red threatened (0,6)->(0,4) and a sandwich against Red (2,4), by moving to (1,5). It is presently safe from a one-move sandwich.
### Our plan
Keep Blue (3,4) secure and dislodge the three opposing center pieces. Target Red (3,3), since Red already has one loss: a Blue landing on (3,2) would capture it against Blue (3,4). Blue (2,3) may stage via (2,2) if safe. Green (1,5) can advance along column 5 to support the center. Check first for any new immediate capture or center threat.

The opponent aggressively fills the center and builds same-color flanks. Expect Red to defend or move (3,3), and Yellow to seek a way to remove Blue (3,4).
### Lessons
Avoid squares that extend an opponent-colored flank through mixed pieces; Green (1,3) would have allowed Red to capture Green and Blue together via a landing on (0,3).

### Position read
Losses: opponent Red 1; our Blue 1 and Green 1; Yellow 0. The opponent holds (3,3), (4,3), and (4,4); our Blue at (3,4) alone prevents center victory. Red captured Blue (2,3). Blue moved (6,7)->(6,4), creating a threat to play (6,4)->(5,4), sandwiching Yellow (4,4) against Blue (3,4).

### Our plan
Keep Blue (3,4) in place. Exploit the threat against Yellow (4,4). Yellow can parry by moving (5,6)->(5,4), blocking the landing square; if so, ensure Blue (6,4) escapes or finds a counter before Yellow can establish a far flank at (7,4). Green should help contest rows 4–5 or clear (1,5), enabling Blue (1,7) to approach (1,4) and threaten Red (2,4) against Blue (3,4).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent aggressively occupies the center and uses same-color sandwich geometry. Expect Yellow to preserve (4,4), likely by blocking (5,4), and Red to protect (2,4)/(3,3) while seeking more Blue losses.

### Lessons
Capture checks require the landing square to touch the captured line; a piece cannot jump through the intended target. Preserve the central Blue because vacating (3,4) allows an immediate opposing center completion.

### Position read
Losses: opponent Red 1; our Blue 1 and Green 1; Yellow 0. The opponent occupies (3,3), (4,3), and (4,4); our Blue at (3,4) prevents center victory. Our Blue at (6,4) can play to (5,4), capturing Yellow (4,4) against Blue (3,4). Green moved (1,5)->(4,5), clearing the row-one lane and adding a center-side anchor.

### Our plan
Keep Blue (3,4) unless the opposing center is decisively broken. On Blue’s next turn, prefer (6,4)->(5,4) to capture Yellow (4,4), unless Red creates a more urgent win threat. Afterward, use Green (4,5) and Green (4,0) to pressure Yellow (4,3), while Blue (1,7) can advance along the cleared first row.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes central occupation and same-color sandwich geometry. Red may try to create a landing square at (3,5) to capture central Blue against Red (3,3). Yellow may retreat (4,3) after losing (4,4), or use (7,4) to contest our Blue on file 4.

### Lessons
Do not place Green on (3,5): Red could land at (3,6) and sandwich Green plus central Blue against Red (3,3). Preserve the central Blue until at least one opposing center piece is removed.

### Position read
Losses after this move: opponent Red 1, Yellow 1; our Blue 1, Green 1. Blue (6,4)->(5,4) captures Yellow (4,4) against Blue (3,4), breaking the opponent’s center threat. The remaining center is Red (3,3), Blue (3,4), Yellow (4,3), with (4,4) empty. Red (3,6) threatens next turn to land at (3,5) and sandwich Blue (3,4) against Red (3,3).

### Our plan
On Green’s turn, if (3,5) remains empty and no greater emergency appears, play Green (4,5)->(3,5) to deny Red’s capture landing and support the center. Keep Blue (3,4) as the center stopper. Seek pressure on Yellow (4,3) using Green’s row-four pieces, while Blue (5,4) provides nearby support.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent aggressively builds central occupation and same-color sandwich flanks. Expect Yellow to refill (4,4), retreat (4,3), or challenge Blue on file 4. Red’s clearest tactical objective is capturing central Blue via (3,5).

### Lessons
Recheck the Red (3,3)/(3,6) sandwich threat every turn. A blocker on (3,5) prevents the immediate capture; do not vacate central Blue while Red and Yellow still threaten center occupation.

### Position read
Losses remain opponent Red 1, Yellow 1; our Blue 1, Green 1. Green (4,5)->(3,5) makes no capture but blocks Red’s immediate (3,6)->(3,5) sandwich of Blue (3,4). Center remains Red (3,3), Blue (3,4), Yellow (4,3), with (4,4) empty. Row 3 now has Red flanks at (3,3)/(3,6) around Blue (3,4) and Green (3,5), but this existing bracket captures nothing unless triggered by a later Red landing.

### Our plan
Keep (3,5) occupied until the Red sandwich geometry is broken. Blue (3,4) remains the essential center stopper. On Blue’s next turn, first check for an immediate opponent center threat or capture; otherwise seek a safe way to pressure Red (3,3) or Yellow (4,3), using Blue (5,4) as support.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes central occupation and same-color sandwich geometry. Expect Red to reposition a flank or attack elsewhere now that (3,5) is unavailable; Yellow may contest (4,4), retreat (4,3), or exploit the newly empty (4,5).

### Lessons
Existing brackets do not capture without a triggering move. Do not vacate Green (3,5) while Red remains at both (3,3) and (3,6), unless Blue (3,4) has first escaped or a flank is removed.

### Position read
Blue (1,7)->(1,4) sandwiches Red (2,4) against Blue (3,4), raising Red to 2 losses. Center remains Red (3,3), Blue (3,4), Yellow (4,3), with (4,4) empty. Green (3,5) still prevents Red from landing there to trigger the row-3 sandwich.

### Our plan
On Green’s turn, check wins and urgent threats first. If (3,2) remains empty and the row is unchanged, Green (3,1)->(3,2) captures Red (3,3) and Blue (3,4) against Green (3,5), eliminating Red at the cost of raising Blue to 2 losses. Yellow can block this by moving (7,2)->(3,2); if so, preserve Blue (3,4) and Green (3,5) while seeking another capture on Red.

Expect Yellow to contest (4,4), block (3,2), or disrupt the planned Green sandwich. The opponent favors central occupation and same-color flank geometry.

### Lessons
Red is now one capture from elimination. Do not vacate Green (3,5) while Red remains at (3,3) and (3,6) unless Blue (3,4) has escaped or a Red flank is removed.

### Position read
Green (3,1)->(3,2) sandwiches Red (3,3) and Blue (3,4) against Green (3,5). Red reaches 3 losses and is eliminated; its survivors become Void. Blue reaches 2 losses and is now one capture from elimination. Center after removal has Yellow at (4,3) and (4,4), with (3,3) and (3,4) empty.

### Our plan
Protect every Blue piece first, especially against Yellow same-color flank landings. On Blue’s next turn, check immediate Yellow threats and seek a safe center entry or capture without exposing a Blue line. Green should retain the (3,2)/(3,5) structure unless moving creates a decisive gain. Prevent Yellow from completing the center.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent has used Yellow to occupy (4,4) and contest the center. Eliminated Red’s Void pieces cannot capture but can move, support Yellow’s center occupation, obstruct lanes, and serve as inert walls.

### Lessons
The planned mixed-line sandwich worked and eliminated one opponent color, but friendly fire put Blue at 2 losses. From now on, losing any Blue piece eliminates that color, so scan every Yellow rook landing before committing.

### Position read
Blue (1,4)->(3,4) sandwiches Yellow (4,4) against Blue (5,4). Yellow reaches 2 losses; Blue also remains at 2, so either normal color is one capture from elimination. We occupy center (3,4); Yellow retains center (4,3). Other Blue pieces are at (3,7), (5,4), and (5,7).

### Our plan
Seek one safe Yellow capture to eliminate its color and win by team elimination, since Red is already eliminated. Protect every Blue piece from Yellow same-color flank landings. Green should create the finishing capture if possible, while preserving Blue’s central support and preventing Yellow/Red Void center occupation.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests the center with Yellow; Red Voids maneuver as blockers, center occupants, and inert walls. Yellow will now prioritize a Blue capture or tactical escape because both active colors are at 2 losses.

### Lessons
Use same-color anchors carefully: the stationary Blue at (5,4) enabled the center capture. Recheck origin vacancies before assuming a sandwich, and avoid friendly-fire lines involving Blue.

### Position read
We hold center squares (3,3) with Green and (3,4) with Blue; the opponent holds (4,4) with Yellow. Blue and Green each have 2 losses, as does Yellow, so any normal-piece capture can eliminate a color. Blue at (5,4) is immediately threatened: Yellow (7,4) can land at (6,4), using Yellow (4,4) as the far flank.

### Our plan
On Blue’s next turn, first remove the (5,4) piece from Yellow’s sandwich geometry unless a winning Yellow capture appears. Preserve our two adjacent upper-center occupants, contest (4,3), and seek one safe capture of Yellow to win by team elimination because the opponent’s other color is already eliminated.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses Yellow to contest center and build same-color flanks; Red Voids maneuver as blockers and inert center occupants. Expect the Red Void at (2,3) to reposition now that (3,3) is blocked.

### Lessons
At two losses, reject any move permitting a one-turn same-color flank. Static sandwiches do nothing until a matching-color normal piece lands, so identify the exact landing square and block or vacate it before that color acts.

### Position read
We occupy (3,3) with Green and (3,4) with Blue; Yellow occupies (4,4). Blue’s threatened piece has shifted from (5,4) to (5,3), escaping Yellow’s (4,4)/(7,4) sandwich geometry. Blue, Green, and Yellow remain at 2 losses, so any capture of a normal piece eliminates that color. Red is eliminated and has Voids at (2,3) and (4,1).

Seek one safe capture of Yellow for immediate team-elimination victory. Preserve every normal piece against one-move Yellow flanks, especially near (4,4). Contest (4,3) while keeping our adjacent upper-center pair intact; Blue at (5,3) is staged below that square.

The opponent uses Yellow to contest center and form same-color sandwiches; Red Voids reposition as blockers and inert center occupants. Expect Yellow to relocate (4,4), occupy (4,3), or create a new flank using the bottom-row pieces.

### Lessons
At two losses, identify the opponent’s exact capture landing squares before every move. Static sandwiches do not capture, but a normal matching-color piece landing on the open flank does.

### Position read
Green’s move from (6,0) to (6,3) sandwiches Blue (5,3) and Yellow (4,3) against Green (3,3). Both reach three losses and are eliminated. Since Red was already eliminated, the opponent has now lost both colors.

### Our plan
The game should end immediately in our team-elimination victory.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent’s Yellow center occupation created a decisive mixed-color sandwich line.

### Lessons
When the opponent is at two losses, a winning sandwich may justify friendly fire—even elimination of our teammate—because eliminating the opponent’s second color ends the game immediately.
